item.title: Europe’s electronic waste crisis holds the key to supply security – if we act on it
item.description: Europe faces a paradox: while dependency on critical raw materials threatens our green transition and strategic autonomy, we are not able to sufficiently recover these very materials in our electronic waste streams. The solution isn’t just better recycling – it requires fundamentally rethinking how we design, use and recover electronics.
item.dc:creator: Aisha Rafique
item.content:encoded: Europe faces a paradox: while dependency on critical raw materials threatens our green transition and strategic autonomy, we are not able to sufficiently recover these very materials in our electronic waste streams. The solution isn’t just better recycling – it requires fundamentally rethinking how we design, use and recover electronics. Electronic waste has grown 82% globally since 2010 , yet Europe recycles less than 20% appropriately. Meanwhile, China controls over 90% of global rare earth processing , and export restrictions from raw material suppliers have increased fivefold since 2009. As the Draghi report warns , demand for critical minerals will quadruple by 2040 – and we continue melting down functional components containing rare earths and strategic materials at 1,500 degrees Celsius, losing their embodied value forever. This destruction represents both environmental and economic waste. Printed circuit boards (PCBAs) and electronic components account for up to 70% of a product’s carbon footprint, despite comprising minimal physical weight. One metric ton of discarded smartphones contains as much gold and copper as 2,000 tons of virgin ore. Yet critical materials and functional components that could serve for decades are lost because conventional pyrometallurgical recycling focuses solely on recovering copper and precious metals such as gold, silver, zinc and lead. The regulatory environment is shifting rapidly. The Critical Raw Materials Act targets 25% of EU consumption from recycled sources by 2030. Extended producer responsibility schemes are tightening. Nevertheless, transformation requires more than compliance. It demands cooperation across the value chain, between manufacturers, waste operators and technology providers. The iPhone recycling robot, Daisy, is seen at an Apple recycling facility in Austin, Texas, U.S. REUTERS/Spencer Selvidge The CIRCUIT project , a collaboration led by Danish Technological Institute, offers one example of this model. Six Danish companies, including electronics manufacturers, PCB suppliers, waste operators and recycling technology, are investigating how increased attention to component removal and repairability could support more circular electronics while maintaining quality standards. The aim is to help technologies integrate with existing logistics while potentially opening new revenue streams. Waste operators may gain access to higher-value material fractions, manufacturers could strengthen component supply chains and differentiate through documented sustainability, and technology providers can benefit from validation with real waste streams. There are three strands to the project. First, we must rescue functional components to support reuse. Many PCBAs are encapsulated in sealings that prevent gentle disassembly. In CIRCUIT, we are investigating methods to safely extract components. Combined with in-depth testing and quality assurance, this creates a verified foundation for recovering reusable components for the purpose of repairability. Second, we need circular design principles embedded from the start. The EU’s Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation will increasingly push manufacturers towards products that are easier to repair, upgrade and disassemble, yet industry still lacks practical frameworks for translating these principles into complex electronics. Rather than treating printed circuit boards as anonymous material streams, we must get better at identifying and extracting components that can extend the lifetime of products already in use. Third, for components unsuitable for reuse, we need alternative recovery methods. New molten salt technology (offered by Nordic Salt Cycle in the CIRCUIT project) operating at 400-600C – versus 1,200-1,500C in conventional smelters – can potentially be the way to go to selectively extract critical materials at a lower cost than existing technologies. A worker at Solenthaler Recycling AG, now soREC AG, checks used mobile phones in a transport box in Gossau, Switzerland. REUTERS/Arnd Wiegmann Europe’s dependencies won’t resolve through mining alone. Even with successful domestic extraction, processing capacity takes years to develop. Meanwhile, our waste already contains materials we desperately need. The question isn’t technological feasibility – pilot projects prove that. It’s whether we can scale solutions before the next supply crisis hits. This requires policy supporting not just collection targets, but also recovery infrastructure. It demands procurement preferences for products designed for circularity. Most crucially, it needs industry to recognise that controlling secondary material flows offers strategic advantages comparable to primary supply access. CIRCUIT shows what this looks like in practice – and aims to offer a blueprint that can be scaled across Europe. The electronic waste that we currently cannot handle represents tomorrow's supply security. Europe has the technical capability, regulatory momentum, and industrial partnerships needed to capture this value. The only question is whether we'll act with the urgency the situation demands – or wait for the next shortage to force our hand. CIRCUIT is a collaboration between El Recycling, Danish Technological Institute, HJHansen Recycling Group, NCAB Group, DEIF, LINAK and Nordic Salt Cycle. It is partially funded by The Danish Environmental Protection Agency and has a total budget of 1.2 million euros.

item.title: Reiche-Sprecher zufrieden mit Gasspeicher-Befüllung: keine Mangellage absehbar
item.description: Das von CDU-Politikerin Katherina Reiche geführte Bundeswirtschaftsministerium ist trotz der niedrigen Stände zufrieden mit der Befüllung der Gasspeicher. Ein Sprecher des Ministeriums sprach am Montag in Berlin von einem guten Füllstand der Speicher. Zudem gebe es neue Terminals, um Flüssiggas (LNG) importieren zu können, und auch Pipeline-Lieferungen aus Norwegen. "Entscheidend ist, die Versorgungssicherheit muss gewährleistet sein. Wir sehen derzeit keine Anzeichen dafür, dass es nicht der Fall ist." Eine Mangellage sei nicht absehbar.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Das von CDU-Politikerin Katherina Reiche geführte Bundeswirtschaftsministerium ist trotz der niedrigen Stände zufrieden mit der Befüllung der Gasspeicher. Ein Sprecher des Ministeriums sprach am Montag in Berlin von einem guten Füllstand der Speicher. Zudem gebe es neue Terminals, um Flüssiggas (LNG) importieren zu können, und auch Pipeline-Lieferungen aus Norwegen. "Entscheidend ist, die Versorgungssicherheit muss gewährleistet sein. Wir sehen derzeit keine Anzeichen dafür, dass es nicht der Fall ist." Eine Mangellage sei nicht absehbar. Die staatlich vorgegebene Befüllung der Gasspeicher auf 70 Prozent bis Anfang November ist nach [USN:L8N44I0KG TEXT:"Einschätzung aus der Energiebranche"] kaum mehr zu schaffen. "Das ist irgendwann physikalisch nicht mehr möglich", sagte die Vorsitzende der Hauptgeschäftsführung des Stromlobbyverbandes BDEW, Kerstin Andreae, am Freitag. Es werde trotz hoher Gaspreise beim Einkauf zwar weiter eingespeichert, aber nur langsam. Noch sei die Vorgabe für die Füllstände erreichbar. "Aber es wird immer enger." Die Bundesnetzagentur sieht die Gasunternehmen in der Pflicht. Auch die Bonner Behörde ist skeptisch, dass die staatliche Vorgabe noch erreicht werden kann. Die Gasspeicher sind derzeit nur etwa zu 50 Prozent gefüllt. Im vergangenen Jahr waren es zum gleichen Zeitpunkt 67 Prozent. Normalerweise können Gashändler im Sommer günstig einkaufen und somit die Speicher füllen, die dann im Winter angezapft werden. Dies ist dieses Jahr aber wegen des Nahost-Krieges, der die Energiepreise nach oben getrieben hat, so nicht möglich. Deswegen zögern viele Firmen. Klaus Müller, Präsident der Bundesnetzagentur, hält die Füllvorgaben für Gasspeicher für überholt. "Die Speichervorgaben haben sich in der Krise bewährt, aber inzwischen drohen die Fehlanreize zu überwiegen. Einen Mehrwert sehe ich nicht mehr", sagte er zuletzt der "Zeit". Die Vorgaben stammen aus dem Jahr 2022, als die Gasmärkte wegen Russlands Angriff auf die Ukraine in Panik gerieten. Der Sprecher des Wirtschaftsministeriums sagte, man habe die Aussagen zur Kenntnis genommen. "Wir haben die geltende Rechtslage." Er habe keine konkreten Änderungspläne mitzuteilen.

item.title: French parliament will need 'serious' budget talks given bond market tensions
item.description: Rising French government borrowing costs will require "serious" talks in parliament on the country's budget, said government spokeswoman Maud Bregeon on Monday, as the government tries to balance cutting the deficit without hurting consumers too much.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Rising French government borrowing costs will require "serious" talks in parliament on the country's budget, said government spokeswoman Maud Bregeon on Monday, as the government tries to balance cutting the deficit without hurting consumers too much. "All of this will clearly require a lot of rigour," said Bregeon, who also reaffirmed that the government would look to improve the public finance situation and reduce the deficit without imposing tax rises on French citizens. The yields on French 10-year government bonds reached their [USN:L1N44G0BA TEXT:"highest"] level since 2008 last week, going above 4.13%. The stage is set for a potentially rocky parliamentary budget battle, as the government seeks to keep the deficit under control ahead of a 2027 presidential election that polls suggest could favour the far right. French Finance Minister Roland Lescure had also [USN:FWN44J01Q TEXT:"said"] earlier on Monday that the government would do all it could to keep the budget deficit as close as possible to 5%. The European Commission has [USN:S8N40A022 TEXT:"forecast"] a 2026 French budget deficit of 5.1%, which would be in breach of EU rules stipulating that countries have a 3% ceiling for their deficit.

item.title: El Kremlin afirma que la ayuda británica en forma de misiles a Ucrania "echa más leña al fuego"
item.description: El Kremlin afirmó el lunes que la decisión de Reino Unido de facilitar a Ucrania información clasificada sobre componentes de fabricación británica utilizados para fabricar misiles de crucero de largo alcance SCALP "echaría más leña al fuego" y que Moscú la consideraba de forma extremadamente negativa.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Kremlin afirmó el lunes que la decisión de Reino Unido de facilitar a Ucrania información clasificada sobre componentes de fabricación británica utilizados para fabricar misiles de crucero de largo alcance SCALP "echaría más leña al fuego" y que Moscú la consideraba de forma extremadamente negativa. El primer ministro británico, Andy Burnham, llegó el lunes a Kiev en su primer viaje al extranjero desde que asumió el cargo y tenía previsto anunciar el apoyo británico para ayudar a Ucrania a mejorar su producción nacional de misiles de largo alcance. Al ser preguntado sobre la visita y el apoyo, el portavoz del Kremlin, Dmitri Peskov, acusó a Reino Unido de hacer todo lo posible para impedir cualquier avance hacia un eventual acuerdo de paz. "Reino Unido está implicada en esta guerra del lado del régimen de Kiev. Reino Unido echa leña al fuego de forma metódica y habitual, y trama planes de forma metódica y habitual para impedir incluso el más mínimo avance en el proceso de resolución pacífica", declaró Peskov a los periodistas. Peskov señaló que el ejército ruso ya estaba recopilando datos de forma sistemática para identificar la ubicación de cualquier instalación de producción de misiles y, a continuación, destruirlas. Moscú advirtió a Londres la semana pasada de "consecuencias" no especificadas por suministrar drones a Kiev, acusando a Reino Unido de profundizar su implicación en la guerra tras un informe según el cual, por primera vez, se habían utilizado drones de fabricación británica para llevar a cabo ataques de largo alcance contra Rusia. Burnham afirmó en ese momento que Londres estaba comprometido a apoyar a Ucrania al 100% contra "esta guerra ilegal".

item.title: India plans first tokenised bond issue in September, sources say
item.description: India will launch tokenised corporate bonds next month, as it tests the use of blockchain technology to enable instant settlement of bond transactions, three sources with direct knowledge of the matter said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Khushi Malhotra
item.content:encoded: India will launch tokenised corporate bonds next month, as it tests the use of blockchain technology to enable instant settlement of bond transactions, three sources with direct knowledge of the matter said on Monday. The notes, to be issued for the first time by state-owned power financier REC (RECM.NS) , would place India alongside markets such as Europe and Hong Kong in using the technology for issuance and settlement. Tokenised bonds are securities whose ownership, issuance, trading and settlement are recorded digitally on a blockchain or distributed ledger, allowing transactions to be completed almost instantly. India's markets regulator and central bank are working together on pushing the technology, according to the sources, who spoke on the condition of anonymity as the discussions are ongoing and confidential. REC will issue tokenised bonds worth less than 5 billion rupees ($57 million) in the offering, the sources said. The offering is expected to be unveiled at an annual financial technology event in Mumbai next month, one of the sources said. India's central bank digital currency will be used to buy the tokenised bonds, one of the sources said. Details about the issuer, timeline and framework have not been reported previously. "The offering would be made available to only a select group of investors at the pilot stage," one of the sources said. Reuters could not ascertain the names of the investors. The central bank, markets regulator and REC did not respond to emails seeking comment. NEW BOND FRAMEWORK To tap the bonds, investors will need to access two digital accounts: a wholesale digital currency wallet provided by a bank, and a new electronic securities wallet, the sources said. Indian depositories are developing an e-wallet, a first of its kind, called DEMAT 2.0, which will record bond holdings on a distributed ledger technology chain. "Subsequent trades can take place only between participants that hold both compatible CBDC and securities wallets," one of the sources said. The bonds will have an initial three-month lock-in and exchanges are expected to develop a secondary market for the tokenised bonds by December, one of the sources said. The securities will not be traded on the conventional electronic book provider platform, the sources said. Depositories NSDL and CDSL did not immediately respond to Reuters queries.

MUMBAI, Aug 24 : India will launch tokenised corporate bonds next month, as it tests the use of blockchain technology to enable instant settlement of bond transactions, three sources with direct knowledge of the matter said on Monday. The notes, to be issued for the first time by state-owned power financier REC, would place India alongside markets such as Europe and Hong Kong in using the technology for issuance and settlement. Tokenised bonds are securities whose ownership, issuance, trading and settlement are recorded digitally on a blockchain or distributed ledger, allowing transactions to be completed almost instantly. India's markets regulator and central bank are working together on pushing the technology, according to the sources, who spoke on the condition of anonymity as the discussions are ongoing and confidential.

REC will issue tokenised bonds worth less than 5 billion rupees ($57 million) in the offering, the sources said. The offering is expected to be unveiled at an annual financial technology event in Mumbai next month, one of the sources said. India's central bank digital currency will be used to buy the tokenised bonds, one of the sources said. Details about the issuer, timeline and framework have not been reported previously. "The offering would be made available to only a select group of investors at the pilot stage," one of the sources said. Reuters could not ascertain the names of the investors. The central bank, markets regulator and REC did not respond to emails seeking comment. NEW BOND FRAMEWORK To tap the bonds, investors will need to access two digital accounts: a wholesale digital currency wallet provided by a bank, and a new electronic securities wallet, the sources said. Indian depositories are developing an e-wallet, a first of its kind, called DEMAT 2.0, which will record bond holdings on a distributed ledger technology chain. "Subsequent trades can take place only between participants that hold both compatible CBDC and securities wallets," one of the sources said. The bonds will have an initial three-month lock-in and exchanges are expected to develop a secondary market for the tokenised bonds by December, one of the sources said. The securities will not be traded on the conventional electronic book provider platform, the sources said. Depositories NSDL and CDSL did not immediately respond to Reuters queries.

item.title: Sterling pauses after four-week rally as investors brace for US sanctions on Iran
item.description: The British pound ticked lower against the dollar on Monday, easing from a four-week rally and as investors braced for a wave of U.S. sanctions on Iran and its trading partners.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The British pound ticked lower against the dollar on Monday, easing from a four-week rally and as investors braced for a wave of [USN:L6N44K07T TEXT:"U.S. sanctions"] on Iran and its trading partners. Sterling dipped nearly 0.1% to $1.3633 by 0956 GMT, after hitting a more than six-month high of $1.3675 on Friday. The pound was flat versus the euro at 85.57 pence to the common currency. The pound is one of the best performing among Group of Seven peers this year, benefiting from market expectations that the Bank of England will hike interest rates towards the end of the year in the face of better-than-expected economic resilience. Traders see benchmark interest rates rising by at least 25 basis points by December, LSEG data showed, although most economists anticipate no change. If pricing shifts to match those expectations, that could weigh on the currency. "The recent combination of resilient growth and easing domestic inflation pressures is encouraging and reinforces our view that there is no need to tighten monetary policy this year," said Maelle Quillevere, an economist at UBS Global Wealth Management, who expects rate cuts could potentially resume in 2027. Providing some relief to concerns about a sluggish economy, economists at the Resolution Foundation think tank said [USN:L8N44J01V TEXT:"economic productivity"] was starting to show signs of sustained improvement, on the back of [USN:L6N44I0UT TEXT:"data last week"] that also pointed to strength among businesses and consumers. Meanwhile, Prime Minister Andy Burnham told European Council President Antonio Costa that London should be [USN:L8N44L0BK TEXT:"bolder in pursuing"] closer ties with the European Union, ahead of a UK-EU summit this year. The Burnham government's first budget in October will be key for investor confidence in Britain, at a time when concerns over elevated sovereign debt levels and higher borrowing costs have rattled bond markets in the U.S. The pound's weakness against the dollar on Monday was also as investors mulled the potential implications of U.S. sanctions on Iran and its trading partners, alongside concerns that it could provoke retaliation from Tehran. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was expected to give a press conference at 1700 GMT.

item.title: Le milliardaire allemand Klaus-Michael Kuehne s'éteint à l'âge de 89 ans
item.description: Le milliardaire allemand Klaus-Michael Kuehne, actionnaire majoritaire du groupe logistique suisse Kuehne+Nagel , est décédé à l'âge de 89 ans, a annoncé lundi la société.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le milliardaire allemand Klaus-Michael Kuehne, actionnaire majoritaire du groupe logistique suisse Kuehne+Nagel (KNIN.S) , est décédé à l'âge de 89 ans, a annoncé lundi la société. Klaus-Michael Kuehne, petit-fils du cofondateur de la société, August Kuehne, détenait également des participations importantes dans les groupes allemands Lufthansa (LHAG.DE) , Hapag-Lloyd (HLAG.DE) et Brenntag (BNRGn.DE) . Il est devenu président du directoire de Kuehne & Nagel en 1975 et a été à la tête de son conseil d'administration de 1992 à 2011.

item.title: Xiaomi develops its own AI mobile chip in challenge to Qualcomm, MediaTek
item.description: The Xring O3 system-on-a-chip advances Xiaomi's in-house semiconductor design efforts with more power-efficient image processing and better artificial intelligence capabilities ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Gao Yuan Xiaomi Corp. launched a mobile processor for its marquee devices, putting pressure on Qualcomm Inc. and MediaTek Inc., which for years supplied the key component to the Chinese company. The Xring O3 system-on-a-chip advances Xiaomi’s in-house semiconductor design efforts with more power-efficient image processing and better artificial intelligence capabilities, the Beijing-based company said in a post on Chinese social media platform Weibo on Monday.  Xiaomi’s new silicon is made using a 3-nanometer fabrication process, according to a WeChat post by founder Lei Jun. That’s closer to the node used for Apple Inc.’s most recent A19 Pro chips and well ahead of its biggest home rival Huawei Technologies Co.’s in-house designs. Xiaomi has contracted Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. to manufacture the chips, Reuters reported. What Bloomberg Intelligence Says Xiaomi’s latest Xring O3 mobile processor stays at 3-nanometer even as leading rivals move to 2nm, which indicates it’s placing more weight on architecture and feature upgrades to drive gains. Redesigned compute, faster memory and stronger on-device AI should help sharpen Xiaomi’s flagship phones’ differentiation, while Xring chips across more devices will help maximize R&D efficiency. Still, limited chip volume suggests Xiaomi will remain heavily reliant on Qualcomm and MediaTek. - Steven Tseng and Rebecca Wang, analysts San Diego, California-based Qualcomm and Taiwan’s MediaTek have long provided Xiaomi’s key processors. The Chinese company, which also designs and produces electric vehicles, is building on years of its own research on semiconductors to lower reliance on foreign chips. Having an in-house chip for its flagship products would strengthen Xiaomi’s bargaining position with suppliers and boost its consumer appeal in a fiercely competitive market. Rival Huawei uses self-developed Kirin processors in its premium phones after a series of US restrictions cut it off from key global suppliers including Qualcomm. In contrast, Xiaomi isn’t subject to sanctions preventing it from contracting with international suppliers. Once China’s No. 1 smartphone maker, Xiaomi is grappling with lackluster demand for both its handset and electric-vehicle businesses as countrywide consumption levels stagnate. In smartphones, the company suffered the heaviest shipment decline among major hardware makers in the June quarter, according to Counterpoint Research. Investors are also concerned that aggressive pricing for its latest sport utility vehicles could further squeeze margins.

item.title: Mapping the Market: Cryptocurrency ether's technical picture brightens after sharp rebound
item.description: Ether lost nearly 70% of its value over the past year, largely as the U.S. dollar strengthened, but technical analysis suggests the tide may be turning for the world's second-largest cryptocurrency.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Romano
item.content:encoded: Ether lost nearly 70% of its value over the past year, largely as the U.S. dollar strengthened, but technical analysis suggests the tide may be turning for the world's second-largest cryptocurrency. Click here for a detailed technical analysis chart. The catalyst was a surprise move by the U.S. Treasury this week: markets turned against the dollar after the U.S. Treasury announced a [USN:L6N44H0LG TEXT:"bond buyback plan"] that weighed on the U.S. currency broadly. As a result, ether has essentially erased all of its fall from April's monthly high. Such a rapid rally, however, rarely continues unchecked. Markets rarely move in a straight line, and the speed of ether's move suggests the market may now have to catch its breath before advancing further. Indeed, the rally has struggled near the April monthly high, which is at $2,464.54, according to data supplied by LSEG. That hesitation points to a possible pause: ether's pullback before surpassing that level indicates it could enter a consolidation phase where its price holds within a band of roughly $2,200-$2,450 as market participants digest the move that lifted it 31% this week from trough to peak. Momentum readings back up this cautious view. The daily Relative Strength Index, a widely used gauge of momentum, is in overbought territory, supporting the notion that ether has entered a "distribution" phase, when early buyers take profits and others enter the market in anticipation of further gains. Should the coin push through resistance, though, the path higher looks clear: a break above the April high could lead traders initially to target the $2,775-$2,825 zone, followed by $3,040-$3,070 and possibly even $3,400-$3,450. On the downside, a fall below $2,200 would undermine the bullish sentiment. What the chart shows: Ether has erased four months of losses this week after a dollar-weakening Treasury announcement Price is consolidating just below the April high of $2,464.54, with resistance capping gains for now A break above that level opens targets at $2,775-$2,825, then $3,040-$3,070, and potentially $3,400-$3,450; a drop below $2,200 would negate the bullish setup (Daily markets commentary from Reuters analysts on the signals financial charts are sending - and what they might mean.)
